doc.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: The Will: big band tribute to Oscar Peterson with Watrous
summary: Berg describes his piece The Will, written for Bill Watrous's big band, which recorded it in two takes in thirty minutes; closing goodbyes.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Was this with the Watrous big band?

Yes. I tried to do something from many different Oscar Peterson projects that I love. And one he did, an album called “Busting Out” with the Ernie Wilkins Big Band, which was a great album. So I thought wouldn’t it be fun to do one big band cut. So I wrote this piece, that’s the title of the album, based on the Gene Lees book, “The Will to Swing.” So this piece is “The Will.” And I play with Bill’s big band and I know that it doesn’t get any better than that. So they came in, they walked in and thirty minutes later they walked out we had an incredible piece of music.
Does that flip you out or what?
Yeah. We had two takes actually. And I could have used either one.
Okay, well I’ll look forward to checking this whole CD out. And I’ll say goodbye again so that we can put it in. So thank you.
